v.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 gets no input, so a conv on edge 4 is cut off and its usual gain vanishes.
Edge 2 starts at node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none, so the usual conv gain disappears.
Removing edge 4 usually hurts, but when node 1 is disconnected the edge carries nothing so the loss is near zero.
Deleting edge 2 normally costs accuracy, but it is already inert when edge 0 is none.
Setting none on an already-none edge changes nothing, versus the usual loss from removing an op.
Setting none on an edge that is already none is a no-op, whereas removing a real op usually hurts.
Filling an empty edge with a strong conv gives a larger gain than swapping an existing op.
Filling an empty edge into the output with a strong conv gives a larger gain than swapping an existing op.

Filling an empty direct input-to-output edge with a strong conv gains more than replacing an existing op.
